summary: A read-it-later service to replace the Pocket that no longer exists: save from a bookmarklet or your phone's share sheet, extract the article with Readability, read it cleanly, tag and search it, import your Pocket export, export everything as JSON, and read offline. This time the reading list is yours.

stack.why: full text over everything you saved
the phone share target needs a public HTTPS URL

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: Your Pocket CSV export, if you made one
prerequisites.why: Phase 5 imports it. The export window closed in November 2025.
prerequisites.get: The CSV Pocket emailed you, if you exported before the shutdown.

prerequisites.name: A phone to install the PWA and use the share sheet
prerequisites.why: Phase 2 saves from the share sheet.
prerequisites.get: Android Chrome supports share targets fully; iOS Safari with the site added to the home screen.

prerequisites.name: A small always-on server (VPS)
prerequisites.why: This needs one process running all the time with a public address.
prerequisites.get: Hetzner Cloud (from about 4 EUR), DigitalOcean or Fly.io. Ubuntu 24.04, the smallest size. You need SSH access and a public IP. Only needed for the deploy phase; develop locally first.

prerequisites.name: A domain or subdomain
prerequisites.get: Register at Cloudflare Registrar, Porkbun or Namecheap, or use a subdomain of one you already own. You add one DNS record in the deploy phase.
prerequisites.cost: roughly $10 a year, or free on an existing domain

prerequisites.name: Caddy on the server
prerequisites.why: Automatic HTTPS in front of the Node process. Without TLS the browser features this relies on (and your visitors' trust) do not work.
prerequisites.get: On the VPS: follow the install steps at caddyserver.com/docs/install for Ubuntu. One Caddyfile with your domain and a reverse_proxy line is the whole config.
prerequisites.verify: caddy version prints a version on the server

env.name: SAVE_TOKEN
env.where: openssl rand -base64 32; carried by the bookmarklet.

env.name: ADMIN_USER
env.where: Any username for the basic-auth admin pages.

env.name: ADMIN_PASS
env.where: Generate one: openssl rand -base64 24. Never reuse a real password.

phases.title: Save and extract
phases.goal: A URL becomes a clean article row; private addresses refused; duplicates update.

steps.do: Tables and POST /save with a timeout, size cap and private-address refusal
steps.detail: articles (id, url unique, title, site, author, published_at, content_html, excerpt, word_count, saved_at, read_at, archived, favorite), tags, article_tags, FTS5.
commands: mkdir reader && cd reader && git init && npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module && npm install @mozilla/readability@0.5 jsdom@25 sanitize-html@2

steps.do: Extract with Readability, sanitize against an allowlist, absolutize URLs

check: A news article saves clean with no scripts
A paywalled page saves what is public with a note
Saving the same URL twice yields one row

phases.title: Capture from anywhere
phases.goal: Bookmarklet, PWA share target, session for the phone.

steps.do: A web app manifest with a share_target posting to /save; a session cookie login

check: A page saves from the desktop bookmarklet
A page saves from a phone share sheet

phases.title: Read
phases.goal: Unread, archive, favorites; a reading page worth reading on.

steps.do: List views and a reading page with measured width, dark mode, font controls
Keyboard shortcuts; mark read on open

check: A long article reads comfortably on a phone
The list updates without reload after archiving

phases.title: Search and tags

steps.do: FTS5 over content synced by triggers
Tags with autocomplete and a tag view

check: A phrase inside a body is found

phases.title: Import and export
phases.goal: The Pocket CSV in, all of it out as JSON.

steps.do: Import the Pocket CSV re-fetching each article with a polite delay
A full JSON export that round-trips

check: A real export imports with tags and read state

phases.title: Offline and deploy
phases.goal: Recent articles readable in airplane mode; backups; service.

steps.do: A service worker caching the last 50 unread

phases.title: Operate it like a product
phases.goal: Only for the product-builder path: know when the reader is down, never lose the database, and keep the server patched.

steps.do: Add a /healthz endpoint and an external uptime check against it
steps.detail: Answer 200 with the build id and a quick database read. Point a free uptime monitor (or your own, from the Healthchecks entry on this site) at it so an outage is noticed before a user notices.

steps.do: Write structured request logs and rotate them
steps.detail: One JSON line per request: method, path, status, duration, no raw IPs. Rotate weekly with logrotate, keep eight.

steps.do: Back the SQLite file up off the machine nightly and test a restore
steps.detail: SQLite's .backup command makes a consistent copy while the app runs. Copy it to object storage or a second machine; then, once, restore it into a fresh checkout and confirm the app reads it.
Firewall allowing only 22, 80 and 443; unattended security updates on; the app running as an unprivileged user under systemd with Restart=on-failure.

check: Stopping the service triggers an uptime alert within a few minutes
A restore from last night's backup contains yesterday's data
A port scan from another machine shows only 22, 80 and 443

product.outcome: A reading list that survives any company's strategy shift, with a phone path and offline reading.

architecture.swap: A different extractor behind the same function

operations.incident: Rotate SAVE_TOKEN if the bookmarklet leaks.

releaseGate: Share-sheet save verified on a phone
Import verified on a real export

notIncluded: Native apps, the recommendation feed, text-to-speech.
after: An RSS feed of your favorites
